name: Heidelberg University
header:
Heidelberg University
Germany · MSc Mathematics; individual doctorate; GAUS network employment route
European research-fit addition.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Pure Mathematics MSc requires German; English-medium UChicago does not remove that requirement.
• Foreign-degree MSc deadline is June 15, not September 30.
• The binding regulations require a motivation document with relevant education/work table.
• LGF 2027 funding is unannounced; doctoral admission itself promises no employment.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Conflict]
MSc accepts a recognized three-year-or-longer mathematics/equivalent bachelor with above-average
performance. The binding regulations allow subject-grade assessment as well as a German2.7 threshold; the
summary instead says better than2.7. A degree with at least50% mathematics needs a mathematics thesis,90
relevant ECTS and16 advanced ECTS in each of two areas; limited conditional admission can remedy up to16
ECTS. UChicago equivalence is individually assessed. Doctorate normally requires master/equivalent; §4(5)-(6)
permits exceptional bachelor graduates to enter a preparatory qualification route or directs them to the MSc.
GAUS jobs require MSc/equivalent. [s1] [s2] [s5] [s6] [s7]
Before submission [Standing rule]
MSc: assess German readiness and degree/credit equivalence, create heiCO account, prepare academic
records and motivation/CV material. For PhD, obtain supervisor agreement, register in heiDOCS and separately
seek faculty acceptance and funding. A supervisor’s willingness or a graduate-school offer does not itself
establish academic eligibility. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
For doctorate, contact an eligible supervisor before faculty application and discuss the bachelor-equivalence
route and funding. GAUS permits naming up to three investigators/projects. MSc has no prior
supervisor-acceptance requirement. Current researchers below are grouped by fit; no one’s 2027 capacity is
assumed. [s5] [s7] [s18] [s19]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
heiCO provides status/email notifications, requested-document reuploads and an “Accept study place offer”
step that opens enrollment. Central guidance says applications/enrollment have been digital-only since June
2025 and certified-copy scans are needed at enrollment. Faculty doctorate separately still requests one email
PDF, a separate thesis PDF, and signed hardcopies after admission; clarify that programme-specific process
rather than assuming central heiCO replaces it. [s5] [s17]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
MSc and GAUS dates are standing rules. Deutschlandstipendium 2026 is closed;2027 unannounced. LGF
explicitly had no 2026 competition and has no 2027 announcement. Current faculty/papers include 2025-26
evidence. [s1] [s7] [s8] [s11]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
MSc with a foreign degree: May 1-June 15 for winter; October 1-November 15 for summer, standing annual
schedule,2027 clock unconfirmed. The later September 30/March 31 domestic dates are not the relevant route
for a UChicago degree. Faculty doctoral acceptance has no annual deadline; decisions typically take1 week-2
months, longer outside term. GAUS open call is rolling. [s1] [s2] [s5] [s7]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
Deutschlandstipendium usually August 1-31 annually; the posted 2026 round has closed and 2027 is not yet
announced. Its FAQ specifies23:59 CEST for references, while the 2026 application page labels its23:59 cutoff
MEZ, a daylight-time inconsistency. GAUS is rolling, without a guaranteed vacancy. LGF had no 2026 call
because of budget cuts;2027 deadline remains unannounced. [s7] [s8] [s9] [s11]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
MSc optional supporting letters belong with the admission file; no separate grace published. GAUS requests
two referee names but zero letters initially. Deutschlandstipendium optional scheme-specific letters must
arrive during the round by its close. LGF requires both professor reports by the same deadline as applicant
materials, when a new call exists. [s2] [s7] [s9] [s12] [s13]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
German DSH-2/equivalent is normally required by enrollment, rather than the mathematics application
deadline; admitted students may receive DSH registration information. No GRE deadline is specified. A doctoral
English/German test deadline is not stated in the faculty entrance checklist. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
MSc supporting materials due with the foreign-degree application. Pending applicants provide at least five
semesters/150 ECTS-equivalent graded work; final qualifying bachelor evidence must arrive by the last
working day before lectures begin. Scholarship documents cannot be added after the competition closes.
Doctoral acceptance requires a complete file before review. [s2] [s5] [s8] [s9]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
MSc offer acceptance and enrollment follow the individual notice and heiCO instructions; no universal 2027
commitment date established. Doctoral employment and fellowships specify their own offer deadlines. No April
15 rule is established for these routes. [s1] [s5] [s17] [s27]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
The pure Mathematics MSc is German, with some English; it requires German proficiency, generally DSH-2 or
accepted equivalent by enrollment. Do not import English-only rules from Scientific Computing or South Asian
Studies. No universal English examination requirement is stated for the individual mathematics doctorate;
clarify with supervisor and doctoral office. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
UChicago’s English-medium degree does not waive the German requirement for the Mathematics MSc. No
mathematics-specific automatic doctoral English waiver policy was found; demonstrate language readiness to
the supervisor/office if requested. [s3] [s4] [s5]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
No requirement in the current MSc regulations, faculty doctoral checklist or GAUS call. Unsolicited score
consideration is not specified. [s2] [s5] [s7]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
MSc: degree/provisional record, transcript, required declaration about prior lost examination rights or ongoing
comparable master examinations, motivation document with relevant education/work chronology, and central
heiCO identity/entrance-qualification uploads as requested. Doctorate: certified degrees/transcripts, dated
signed CV, photoID showing birthplace, signed application/agreement and enrollment form; foreign-degree
applicants also provide relevant course achievements and master-level thesis separately. [s2] [s5] [s17]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
No mathematics-specific course spreadsheet is prescribed. Academic records must demonstrate subject
content and equivalence; the doctoral foreign-degree route explicitly asks for relevant course achievements.
The separate computer-science course-summary form is not a mathematics requirement. [s2] [s5]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No universal separate syllabus upload or length limit is stated for mathematics. Prepare descriptions to
establish foreign-course equivalence if the committee requests them; do not substitute course titles for needed
content evidence. [s2] [s5]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
MSc: no mandatory count; supporting recommendations are optional under the regulations. Faculty PhD
acceptance: signed supervisor agreement, not a fixed external-letter count. GAUS: two referee names, zero
initial letters. LGF: exactly two professor reports for a new application. Deutschlandstipendium: optional
scheme-specific letters, no required count. [s2] [s5] [s7] [s9] [s12]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
LGF adds two confidential form reports, ideally one from the supervisor. They assess relationship, course/exam
grades, research aptitude (12 lines), peer comparison, project content/method/significance, timetable (10
lines), and additional comments/ranking (35 lines). Deutschlandstipendium letters must explicitly address that
scholarship; generic reused letters are not accepted under its FAQ. [s9] [s14]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
No automatic referee invitation is documented. GAUS stores referee names for possible later requests. LGF
applicant sends the form and identification number/email to evaluators; they upload directly.
Deutschlandstipendium allows applicant upload or direct referee email to
deutschlandstipendium@uni-heidelberg.de. [s7] [s9] [s12] [s14]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
LGF does not require waiting for all applicant attachments: register first and coordinate reports with the
identification number, or personal email if the number is not yet available. GAUS initially asks only for referee
details. No submit-first automated trigger is established for optional MSc/scholarship letters. [s7] [s9] [s13]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
LGF sends an automatic email for each report received; two receipt emails are needed for a new application.
The ordinary heiCO portal shows application status, but that does not establish a separate optional-letter
checklist. GAUS email-letter receipt confirmation is not promised. [s7] [s12] [s17]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
LGF applicant PDF can be replaced before the deadline and only its latest version counts; evaluator-report
replacement/reuse is not expressly guaranteed. Deutschlandstipendium letters must be written for that
competition and received within its application window. Other cross-cycle letter reuse is unverified. [s9] [s13]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
MSc motivation document must include a table of relevant education/work stages; a separate CV upload may
be specified in heiCO. Doctoral faculty CV must be dated and signed. GAUS requires CV; LGF requires a tabular
CV. No public universal page/font limit for these CVs. [s2] [s5] [s7] [s12]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
MSc requires a motivation letter with a tabular chronology of education/employment relevant to the
programme, optionally supported by evidence such as recommendations (translation/paraphrase of §2(4)). No
word/page limit is published. GAUS requires a cover letter identifying research interests, up to three preferred
investigators and projects; no length limit stated. [s2] [s7]
Personal / background statement; Publications list [Standing rule]
No separate mandatory item in this category is listed for ordinary MSc/faculty PhD admission or the GAUS PhD
call. Do not import the GAUS postdoctoral publication-list requirement. Scholarship motivation/background
information is covered separately below. [s2] [s5] [s7]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
GAUS cover letter records research interests and preferred projects/advisers; no separate research-interest
essay is required. Faculty PhD forms identify the project and supervisor. Ordinary MSc has no distinct
research-interest statement beyond motivation. [s2] [s5] [s7]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
LGF, if reopened: project outline at most5 pages, bibliography at most5 pages and completion schedule at
most1 page; guideline font10-12pt and1.5-line spacing. English is accepted. Combine attachments into one
PDF<=10MB. Ordinary MSc has no proposal requirement; doctoral supervisor/individual job may add one. [s2]
[s12] [s13]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Faculty PhD applicants with foreign degrees supply their final master-level thesis as a separate PDF; ask what
substitutes under a bachelor exception. GAUS requests master thesis/preliminary version/equivalent within the
single application PDF. No ordinary MSc writing sample is prescribed. [s2] [s5] [s7]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
No additional mathematics-course essay/form beyond academic records. Supply relevant-course evidence for
foreign-degree doctoral assessment. [s2] [s5]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium field “Darstellung der Motivation”:2500 characters including spaces. In paraphrase,
explain how academic achievement, awards, practical experience and service, in personal/family context,
predict outstanding study/career performance. Do not upload an extra motivation letter; it is ignored. Submit
degree/current transcript, German-grade conversion and evidence for claimed achievements/circumstances.
LGF requires the proposal/timetable/bibliography/CV and qualification/acceptance documents described above.
[s8] [s9] [s12] [s13]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
MSc examination-status declaration and doctoral official forms are required. GAUS sends its complete
application as one PDF<=5MB to applications.crc326gaus@math.uni-frankfurt.de. LGF referees should save
the PDF form locally and use Adobe Reader on macOS to avoid form-data compatibility problems. [s2] [s5] [s7]
[s14]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
No guaranteed MSc stipend. Deutschlandstipendium: EUR300/month, EUR3600/year. GAUS salary uses TV-L
E13, but workload percentage/step and annual amount are not specified in the open call. LGF standing amount
EUR1650/month including EUR100 materials/travel, EUR19,800/12months by arithmetic; it is not an available
2027 award yet. [s7] [s10] [s11]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium generally two semesters with conditional renewal. LGF up to three years if a
competition resumes. GAUS employment term is vacancy-specific. Academic doctoral acceptance for five years
does not imply a five-year funded contract. [s5] [s7] [s9] [s11]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium accepts all nationalities and incoming MSc students, conditional on enrollment;
doctoral students are excluded. GAUS supports international applicants. LGF permits foreign qualifying
degrees, but faculty doctoral acceptance must be established before applying; a supervisor letter alone is
insufficient. [s7] [s8] [s9] [s13]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium is competitive and generally incompatible with other merit-based cash awards
averaging>=EUR30/month. LGF is a fellowship rather than employment; previous overlapping fellowships and
recent related Heidelberg employment can affect eligibility, and secondary work is restricted. Confirm the rules
when a new call opens. [s8] [s11] [s13]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
MSc admission, Deutschlandstipendium and LGF are separate applications. Doctoral faculty acceptance and an
employment offer are also separate. LGF registration alone is incomplete without the applicant PDF and two
reports. [s5] [s8] [s12]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Supervisor/project employment, external DAAD/foundation scholarships and Graduate Academy grants are
possible. LGF health-insurance allowance can cover50% of actual cost up toEUR100/month; child allowances
are also available under standing rules. Completion/mobility grants are not guaranteed incoming full-degree
support. [s13] [s28]
Application fee [Standing rule]
University states there is no application fee. Current non-EU MSc tuition EUR1500/semester plus EUR189.80
semester contribution (winter 2026-27); older faculty estimates nearEUR170 are stale. These are
enrollment/study costs, not application fees.2027 rates need reconfirmation. [s3] [s15] [s16]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
No application-fee waiver needed under the stated zero-fee policy. International tuition exemptions are
separate, based on qualifying status and evidence; UChicago/F-1 alone does not establish one. [s3] [s16]

text:
Heidelberg University
Germany · MSc Mathematics; individual doctorate; GAUS network employment route
European research-fit addition.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Pure Mathematics MSc requires German; English-medium UChicago does not remove that requirement.
• Foreign-degree MSc deadline is June 15, not September 30.
• The binding regulations require a motivation document with relevant education/work table.
• LGF 2027 funding is unannounced; doctoral admission itself promises no employment.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Conflict]
MSc accepts a recognized three-year-or-longer mathematics/equivalent bachelor with above-average
performance. The binding regulations allow subject-grade assessment as well as a German2.7 threshold; the
summary instead says better than2.7. A degree with at least50% mathematics needs a mathematics thesis,90
relevant ECTS and16 advanced ECTS in each of two areas; limited conditional admission can remedy up to16
ECTS. UChicago equivalence is individually assessed. Doctorate normally requires master/equivalent; §4(5)-(6)
permits exceptional bachelor graduates to enter a preparatory qualification route or directs them to the MSc.
GAUS jobs require MSc/equivalent. [s1] [s2] [s5] [s6] [s7]
Before submission [Standing rule]
MSc: assess German readiness and degree/credit equivalence, create heiCO account, prepare academic
records and motivation/CV material. For PhD, obtain supervisor agreement, register in heiDOCS and separately
seek faculty acceptance and funding. A supervisor’s willingness or a graduate-school offer does not itself
establish academic eligibility. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
For doctorate, contact an eligible supervisor before faculty application and discuss the bachelor-equivalence
route and funding. GAUS permits naming up to three investigators/projects. MSc has no prior
supervisor-acceptance requirement. Current researchers below are grouped by fit; no one’s 2027 capacity is
assumed. [s5] [s7] [s18] [s19]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
heiCO provides status/email notifications, requested-document reuploads and an “Accept study place offer”
step that opens enrollment. Central guidance says applications/enrollment have been digital-only since June
2025 and certified-copy scans are needed at enrollment. Faculty doctorate separately still requests one email
PDF, a separate thesis PDF, and signed hardcopies after admission; clarify that programme-specific process
rather than assuming central heiCO replaces it. [s5] [s17]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
MSc and GAUS dates are standing rules. Deutschlandstipendium 2026 is closed;2027 unannounced. LGF
explicitly had no 2026 competition and has no 2027 announcement. Current faculty/papers include 2025-26
evidence. [s1] [s7] [s8] [s11]

Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Standing rule]
MSc with a foreign degree: May 1-June 15 for winter; October 1-November 15 for summer, standing annual
schedule,2027 clock unconfirmed. The later September 30/March 31 domestic dates are not the relevant route
for a UChicago degree. Faculty doctoral acceptance has no annual deadline; decisions typically take1 week-2
months, longer outside term. GAUS open call is rolling. [s1] [s2] [s5] [s7]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
Deutschlandstipendium usually August 1-31 annually; the posted 2026 round has closed and 2027 is not yet
announced. Its FAQ specifies23:59 CEST for references, while the 2026 application page labels its23:59 cutoff
MEZ, a daylight-time inconsistency. GAUS is rolling, without a guaranteed vacancy. LGF had no 2026 call
because of budget cuts;2027 deadline remains unannounced. [s7] [s8] [s9] [s11]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
MSc optional supporting letters belong with the admission file; no separate grace published. GAUS requests
two referee names but zero letters initially. Deutschlandstipendium optional scheme-specific letters must
arrive during the round by its close. LGF requires both professor reports by the same deadline as applicant
materials, when a new call exists. [s2] [s7] [s9] [s12] [s13]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
German DSH-2/equivalent is normally required by enrollment, rather than the mathematics application
deadline; admitted students may receive DSH registration information. No GRE deadline is specified. A doctoral
English/German test deadline is not stated in the faculty entrance checklist. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
MSc supporting materials due with the foreign-degree application. Pending applicants provide at least five
semesters/150 ECTS-equivalent graded work; final qualifying bachelor evidence must arrive by the last
working day before lectures begin. Scholarship documents cannot be added after the competition closes.
Doctoral acceptance requires a complete file before review. [s2] [s5] [s8] [s9]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
MSc offer acceptance and enrollment follow the individual notice and heiCO instructions; no universal 2027
commitment date established. Doctoral employment and fellowships specify their own offer deadlines. No April
15 rule is established for these routes. [s1] [s5] [s17] [s27]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
The pure Mathematics MSc is German, with some English; it requires German proficiency, generally DSH-2 or
accepted equivalent by enrollment. Do not import English-only rules from Scientific Computing or South Asian
Studies. No universal English examination requirement is stated for the individual mathematics doctorate;
clarify with supervisor and doctoral office. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
UChicago’s English-medium degree does not waive the German requirement for the Mathematics MSc. No
mathematics-specific automatic doctoral English waiver policy was found; demonstrate language readiness to
the supervisor/office if requested. [s3] [s4] [s5]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
No requirement in the current MSc regulations, faculty doctoral checklist or GAUS call. Unsolicited score
consideration is not specified. [s2] [s5] [s7]

Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
MSc: degree/provisional record, transcript, required declaration about prior lost examination rights or ongoing
comparable master examinations, motivation document with relevant education/work chronology, and central
heiCO identity/entrance-qualification uploads as requested. Doctorate: certified degrees/transcripts, dated
signed CV, photoID showing birthplace, signed application/agreement and enrollment form; foreign-degree
applicants also provide relevant course achievements and master-level thesis separately. [s2] [s5] [s17]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
No mathematics-specific course spreadsheet is prescribed. Academic records must demonstrate subject
content and equivalence; the doctoral foreign-degree route explicitly asks for relevant course achievements.
The separate computer-science course-summary form is not a mathematics requirement. [s2] [s5]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No universal separate syllabus upload or length limit is stated for mathematics. Prepare descriptions to
establish foreign-course equivalence if the committee requests them; do not substitute course titles for needed
content evidence. [s2] [s5]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
MSc: no mandatory count; supporting recommendations are optional under the regulations. Faculty PhD
acceptance: signed supervisor agreement, not a fixed external-letter count. GAUS: two referee names, zero
initial letters. LGF: exactly two professor reports for a new application. Deutschlandstipendium: optional
scheme-specific letters, no required count. [s2] [s5] [s7] [s9] [s12]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
LGF adds two confidential form reports, ideally one from the supervisor. They assess relationship, course/exam
grades, research aptitude (12 lines), peer comparison, project content/method/significance, timetable (10
lines), and additional comments/ranking (35 lines). Deutschlandstipendium letters must explicitly address that
scholarship; generic reused letters are not accepted under its FAQ. [s9] [s14]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
No automatic referee invitation is documented. GAUS stores referee names for possible later requests. LGF
applicant sends the form and identification number/email to evaluators; they upload directly.
Deutschlandstipendium allows applicant upload or direct referee email to
deutschlandstipendium@uni-heidelberg.de. [s7] [s9] [s12] [s14]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
LGF does not require waiting for all applicant attachments: register first and coordinate reports with the
identification number, or personal email if the number is not yet available. GAUS initially asks only for referee
details. No submit-first automated trigger is established for optional MSc/scholarship letters. [s7] [s9] [s13]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
LGF sends an automatic email for each report received; two receipt emails are needed for a new application.
The ordinary heiCO portal shows application status, but that does not establish a separate optional-letter
checklist. GAUS email-letter receipt confirmation is not promised. [s7] [s12] [s17]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
LGF applicant PDF can be replaced before the deadline and only its latest version counts; evaluator-report
replacement/reuse is not expressly guaranteed. Deutschlandstipendium letters must be written for that
competition and received within its application window. Other cross-cycle letter reuse is unverified. [s9] [s13]

Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
MSc motivation document must include a table of relevant education/work stages; a separate CV upload may
be specified in heiCO. Doctoral faculty CV must be dated and signed. GAUS requires CV; LGF requires a tabular
CV. No public universal page/font limit for these CVs. [s2] [s5] [s7] [s12]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
MSc requires a motivation letter with a tabular chronology of education/employment relevant to the
programme, optionally supported by evidence such as recommendations (translation/paraphrase of §2(4)). No
word/page limit is published. GAUS requires a cover letter identifying research interests, up to three preferred
investigators and projects; no length limit stated. [s2] [s7]
Personal / background statement; Publications list [Standing rule]
No separate mandatory item in this category is listed for ordinary MSc/faculty PhD admission or the GAUS PhD
call. Do not import the GAUS postdoctoral publication-list requirement. Scholarship motivation/background
information is covered separately below. [s2] [s5] [s7]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
GAUS cover letter records research interests and preferred projects/advisers; no separate research-interest
essay is required. Faculty PhD forms identify the project and supervisor. Ordinary MSc has no distinct
research-interest statement beyond motivation. [s2] [s5] [s7]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
LGF, if reopened: project outline at most5 pages, bibliography at most5 pages and completion schedule at
most1 page; guideline font10-12pt and1.5-line spacing. English is accepted. Combine attachments into one
PDF<=10MB. Ordinary MSc has no proposal requirement; doctoral supervisor/individual job may add one. [s2]
[s12] [s13]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Faculty PhD applicants with foreign degrees supply their final master-level thesis as a separate PDF; ask what
substitutes under a bachelor exception. GAUS requests master thesis/preliminary version/equivalent within the
single application PDF. No ordinary MSc writing sample is prescribed. [s2] [s5] [s7]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
No additional mathematics-course essay/form beyond academic records. Supply relevant-course evidence for
foreign-degree doctoral assessment. [s2] [s5]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium field “Darstellung der Motivation”:2500 characters including spaces. In paraphrase,
explain how academic achievement, awards, practical experience and service, in personal/family context,
predict outstanding study/career performance. Do not upload an extra motivation letter; it is ignored. Submit
degree/current transcript, German-grade conversion and evidence for claimed achievements/circumstances.
LGF requires the proposal/timetable/bibliography/CV and qualification/acceptance documents described above.
[s8] [s9] [s12] [s13]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
MSc examination-status declaration and doctoral official forms are required. GAUS sends its complete
application as one PDF<=5MB to applications.crc326gaus@math.uni-frankfurt.de. LGF referees should save
the PDF form locally and use Adobe Reader on macOS to avoid form-data compatibility problems. [s2] [s5] [s7]
[s14]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
No guaranteed MSc stipend. Deutschlandstipendium: EUR300/month, EUR3600/year. GAUS salary uses TV-L
E13, but workload percentage/step and annual amount are not specified in the open call. LGF standing amount
EUR1650/month including EUR100 materials/travel, EUR19,800/12months by arithmetic; it is not an available
2027 award yet. [s7] [s10] [s11]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium generally two semesters with conditional renewal. LGF up to three years if a
competition resumes. GAUS employment term is vacancy-specific. Academic doctoral acceptance for five years
does not imply a five-year funded contract. [s5] [s7] [s9] [s11]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium accepts all nationalities and incoming MSc students, conditional on enrollment;
doctoral students are excluded. GAUS supports international applicants. LGF permits foreign qualifying
degrees, but faculty doctoral acceptance must be established before applying; a supervisor letter alone is
insufficient. [s7] [s8] [s9] [s13]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Deutschlandstipendium is competitive and generally incompatible with other merit-based cash awards
averaging>=EUR30/month. LGF is a fellowship rather than employment; previous overlapping fellowships and
recent related Heidelberg employment can affect eligibility, and secondary work is restricted. Confirm the rules
when a new call opens. [s8] [s11] [s13]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
MSc admission, Deutschlandstipendium and LGF are separate applications. Doctoral faculty acceptance and an
employment offer are also separate. LGF registration alone is incomplete without the applicant PDF and two
reports. [s5] [s8] [s12]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Supervisor/project employment, external DAAD/foundation scholarships and Graduate Academy grants are
possible. LGF health-insurance allowance can cover50% of actual cost up toEUR100/month; child allowances
are also available under standing rules. Completion/mobility grants are not guaranteed incoming full-degree
support. [s13] [s28]
Application fee [Standing rule]
University states there is no application fee. Current non-EU MSc tuition EUR1500/semester plus EUR189.80
semester contribution (winter 2026-27); older faculty estimates nearEUR170 are stale. These are
enrollment/study costs, not application fees.2027 rates need reconfirmation. [s3] [s15] [s16]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
No application-fee waiver needed under the stated zero-fee policy. International tuition exemptions are
separate, based on qualifying status and evidence; UChicago/F-1 alone does not establish one. [s3] [s16]
